subject: English
passage: Overuse of agricultural land by European starlings has caused many grasslands across the Midwest to be replaced by degraded pastures—areas stripped of native vegetation and dominated by invasive starling flocks. Starlings in degraded areas persist in a state of poor health that reduces their nutritional value—and thus their appeal—to many predators. Nawal Hafez and colleagues placed red-tailed hawks, a once-common predator species experiencing significant population declines in recent years, in enclosures that each contained a nutritionally poor and a nutritionally rich European starling. The researchers found that the hawks selected the nutritionally rich starling in 44.2% of trials and the nutritionally poor starling in 39.1% of trials, suggesting that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: red-tailed hawks do not always avoid foraging on nutritionally poor starlings, making red-tailed hawk population recovery a potentially important tool for controlling degraded pastures.
choices.B: red-tailed hawks are willing to hunt starlings, but if given a choice, they will prey on other more nutritious bird species instead.
choices.C: red-tailed hawks are reluctant to feed on both nutritionally poor and nutritionally rich starlings and are therefore unlikely to thrive in grasslands.
choices.D: red-tailed hawks are less likely to consume starlings in degraded areas than other species of raptors are, putting red-tailed hawks at a high risk of extinction.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it presents the conclusion that most logically follows from the text's discussion of the researchers' findings about European starlings and red-tailed hawks. The text explains that degraded pastures are areas that used to be grasslands but are now dominated by European starling flocks. The text suggests that because native vegetation has been stripped from those areas, the starlings exist in a state of poor health that makes them less nutritional for many predators. The text goes on to explain that in a study with a choice between two European starlings, red-tailed hawks (a predator species that has been significantly declining) consumed a nutritionally rich starling 44.2% of the time and a nutritionally poor starling 39.1% of the time. Because the red-tailed hawks didn't always avoid consuming nutritionally poor starlings, even when nutritionally rich ones were available, it follows that helping red-tailed hawk populations to grow could help control degraded pastures by increasing the number of hawks that may consume and thus remove nutritionally poor European starlings from degraded areas.

Why C is incorrect:

Choice C is incorrect because the text doesn't suggest that red-tailed hawks are generally reluctant to feed on starlings. In fact, the text indicates that the red-tailed hawks in the study did consume starlings, feeding on both nutritionally poor and nutritionally rich ones.
